patient_summary:
Hello there! I'm here to tell you about what happened during your eye exam and what you need to know about your medicines. 

You had a complete eye exam today. The doctor checked your eyes and found everything was normal. You didn't have any problems with your eyes or vision. 

You were prescribed some medicines by your doctor. One of them is called amoxicillin-clavulanate. It comes in a chewable tablet and a tablet that you take by mouth. The chewable tablet has 125 mg of amoxicillin and 31.25 mg of clavulanate. The tablet you take by mouth has 0.5 mg of adrenocot. You need to take the chewable tablet twice a day, which means you should take it in the morning and in the evening.

The doctor also gave you a tablet called Vioxx. It comes in a tablet that you take by mouth. Each tablet has 12.5 mg of Vioxx. You also need to take this twice a day, in the morning and in the evening.

You told the doctor you have allergies to aspirin. This can make you feel disoriented and cause upset in your tummy. You need to be careful with aspirin and talk to your doctor if you ever take it.

The doctor also told you to come back to the clinic in 12 months for another check-up. 

If you ever feel fever, headache, nausea, or dizziness, you should tell your doctor right away. These could be signs of something else that needs to be checked. 

Remember to take your medicines as the doctor told you. If you have any questions, you can always ask your doctor or nurse.
caregiver_checklist: Check patient’s temperature, headache, nausea, and dizziness every hour for the first 6 hours.
Call the patient’s healthcare provider if symptoms persist or worsen.
Schedule a follow-up appointment in 12 months.
Watch for signs of aspirin allergy such as disorientation or GI upset.
Call the healthcare provider if the patient experiences any of these symptoms.
Monitor for signs of amoxicillin-clavulanate side effects like rash, itching, or difficulty breathing.
Schedule a return eye examination in 12 months.
Call the healthcare provider if vision changes or new symptoms develop.
Medication: aspirin | dose: 125 mg | how often: BID (twice a day)
Medication: amoxicillin-clavulanate | dose: 125 mg, 31.25 mg, 0.5 mg, 12.5 mg | how often: BID (twice a day)
child_explanation: You had some tummy troubles and a stuffy nose. Now you need a special eye check-up. Your grown-ups and doctors are taking good care of you. They gave you medicine to help your tummy feel better. You'll see the doctor in a few days. Everything looks fine, you're just feeling a bit off.
